# ApplicationBase

**Class:** `UltraCanvasApplicationBase` · **Group:** [Application, windows and dialogs](../Groups/Application-Windows-And-Dialogs.md) · **Header:** [`UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasApplication.h`](../../../UltraCanvas/include/UltraCanvasApplication.h) · `#include "UltraCanvasApplication.h"`

## What it is for

The application: initialisation, the event loop (`Run`), exit, timers, the clipboard and the windows it owns. Construct `UltraCanvasApplication` (the platform's subclass) once in `main`.

- [UltraCanvasDialogKeyboard](../../UltraCanvas/UltraCanvasDialogKeyboard.md)

## Creating it

Constructors:

```cpp
UltraCanvasApplicationBase();
```

The first string argument is always the element's **identifier**, never its text (see [Core concepts](../Core-Concepts.md#identifiers)).

## Callbacks

Assign a lambda to the member (or call the setter). Capture the element and its parents **raw**, never as a `shared_ptr` - see [Events and callbacks](../Events-and-Callbacks.md#ownership).

| Callback | Signature | When it fires |
|---|---|---|
| `PostToUIThread()` | `void PostToUIThread(std::function<void()> task)` | Schedules `task` to run on the main / UI thread the next time the event loop iterates. Safe to call from any thread, including a libcurl async worker (UltraNet_HttpRequestAsync callback) or any std::thread the app spawns. The call is non-blocking; the task runs after the loop wakes (WakeUpEventLoop is signalled here … |
| `RegisterEventLoopRunCallback()` | `void RegisterEventLoopRunCallback(std::function<void()> callback)` | Takes a callback. |
| `StartTimer()` | `TimerId StartTimer(unsigned int milliseconds_interval, bool periodic, std::function<void(TimerId)> callback = nullptr)` | Timer API - timers fire on the main thread |
| `AddFdWatch()` | `FdWatchId AddFdWatch(int fd, FdWatchType type, std::function<void()> callback)` | Watch `fd` for readability/writability from within the event loop. The callback runs on the UI thread on each iteration the fd is ready. Returns an id for RemoveFdWatch(). Used by host integrations that must service their own sockets (e.g. IPC) on the toolkit's loop. Thread-safe. |
| `SetThemeProvider()` | `void SetThemeProvider(std::function<UltraCanvasTheme(const HostAppearance&)> provider)` | Takes a callback. |
| `onApplicationExitRequest` | `std::function<bool()> onApplicationExitRequest` | _Application exit request_ |
| `onApplicationExit` | `std::function<void()> onApplicationExit` | _Application exit_ |

## Option types in this header

### struct `SystemFontScanStatus`

How the system fonts' background scan went, for a start-up report.

| Field | Declaration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `started` | `bool started = false` | a scan was started (Windows, generated config) |
| `finished` | `bool finished = false` | it has ended |
| `succeeded` | `bool succeeded = false` | ... with a usable font set |
| `adoptedAtStart` | `bool adoptedAtStart = false` | its set was current before the first window |
| `ms` | `double ms = 0` | how long it took, once finished |

### enum `FdWatchType`

Watches a file descriptor from within the UltraCanvas event loop. Added so a host integration (e.g. Ladybird's IPC to its WebContent process) can have its sockets serviced by the same wait the toolkit already runs, instead of needing a second event loop. Registered via UltraCanvasApplicationBase::AddFdWatch().

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Read` |  |
| `Write` |  |

### struct `StartupStageTiming`

One step of UltraCanvasApplicationBase::Initialize() and how long it took (see GetStartupTimings).

| Field | Declaration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `stage` | `std::string stage` |  |
| `ms` | `double ms = 0` |  |

### struct `FdWatch`

File-descriptor watches (see FdWatchType). Registered via AddFdWatch(); the platform event loop folds these fds into its native wait primitive (Linux: the select() in CollectAndProcessNativeEvents) and calls FireFdWatch() for each fd that became ready.

| Field | Declaration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `FdWatchId id` |  |
| `fd` | `int fd` |  |
| `type` | `FdWatchType type` |  |
| `callback` | `std::function<void()> callback` |  |

### struct `FdWatchKey`

(fd,type,id) view used by platform loops to build the wait set without copying callbacks; FireFdWatch() runs the callback for a ready watch.

| Field | Declaration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `FdWatchId id` |  |
| `fd` | `int fd` |  |
| `type` | `FdWatchType type` |  |

### struct `TouchPoint`

Backends deliver raw per-finger touches; turning two of them into a pinch/rotate is pure geometry, so it lives here rather than in each backend - every touch platform gets it from one implementation.

| Field | Declaration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pointerId` | `int pointerId = 0` |  |
| `position` | `Point2Di position` |  |
